info.name: StartupKaro API
info.description:
# StartupKaro API

Services marketplace backend. Customers browse a catalog (categories: **Bundles / Start / Manage / Protect**), pay via **Razorpay**, and track orders; advisors handle quote-based work.

## Two service types → two CTAs
Each service has a `type` (`fixed | bundle | quote`); the catalog exposes a `cta`:

**fixed / bundle → `cta: fixed`** — self-serve checkout. Customer `Purchases > Initiate` → Razorpay Checkout → `Verify` (webhook `payment.captured` is the source of truth). Price is tax-exclusive; **18% GST added at checkout**.

**quote → `cta: quote`** — no self-serve payment. Customer submits an `Inquiry` → an employee negotiates → creates a customer (if needed) → creates an **admin order** at the agreed amount → settles it.

## Orders, part payments & settlement
An order holds the agreed **total**; `payments` is a ledger of receipts. `amountPaid` / `amountDue` / `paymentState` (`unpaid|partially_paid|paid`) are derived. **Part payments** are supported (common in India): via a Razorpay **Payment Link** with `acceptPartial` (single or milestone links) or **offline** receipts logged by an admin. The order confirms on the **first** payment. Payment links have a default **7-day expiry**; webhooks (`payment_link.paid` / `payment_link.partially_paid` / `payment_link.expired`) keep records in sync.

## Bundles
Managed via **Admin > Bundles** (create/update/get/delete): a bundle is a service (type=bundle) plus its line-items, edited in one payload. They surface in the public catalog under the Bundles category.

## Analytics
**Admin > Analytics**: revenue, orders, by-service, payment health.

## Setup
1. **Admin > Auth > Login** — admin tokens auto-populate.
2. **Customer > Auth > Signup/Login** — customer tokens auto-populate.
3. IDs (service, bundle, order, customer, inquiry, payment link) auto-save from responses.

item.name: Invoices
item.description:
Invoices are issued **automatically when an order moves to `completed`**. There is no invoice before fulfilment.

Numbering is a gapless per-financial-year series (`SK/26-27/0001`). Party details and line items are snapshotted at issue time, so later edits to an address or the service catalog never alter an already-issued invoice.

All money is in **paise** (2950000 = ₹29,500.00).

optional, ISO datetime — issuedAt upper bound

Paginated, newest first. Filter by supply type to separate CGST+SGST invoices from IGST ones.

query.description: optional, format YYYY-YY — omit for all time

request.description:
Tax collected grouped by place of supply and supply type. GST is filed per state, so the summary groups the same way rather than reporting one lump figure.

All money is in **paise** (2950000 = ₹29,500.00).

**Tax split.** Indian states do not have different GST *rates* — the rate is uniform. What differs is the split, decided by the buyer's `stateCode` against Punjab (03):
- Punjab → `intra_state` → `cgst` + `sgst` populated, `igst` = 0
- elsewhere → `inter_state` → `igst` populated, `cgst`/`sgst` = 0

`taxableValue + totalTax == total` always holds, enforced by a DB constraint.

All money is in **paise** (2950000 = ₹29,500.00).

request.description: ⚠️ **Breaking change:** takes an **invoice id**. The previous `/admin/invoices/order/:orderId/download` path has been removed — resolve the order via *Get Invoice by Order* first, or use the id from *List Invoices*.

**Admin role required.**

Completing an order issues its invoice automatically, so this is the backfill path for orders that were completed before invoicing existed.

**Idempotent** — an order that already has an invoice returns the existing one rather than burning a second number on the same supply.

Backfill oldest-first: numbers are assigned in call order, so issuing out of order leaves the series' dates and numbers disagreeing.

Create a customer account with email + password and sign in immediately. Works alongside Google and phone-OTP sign-in.

**Body**
- `name` — required
- `email` — required, unique
- `password` — required, min 8 characters
- `phone` — optional; self-entered, so stored **unverified**

Returns `{ status: "authenticated", tokens, user }`. A duplicate email or phone returns 409.

response.name: 409 Already Registered

request.description:
Sign in with email + password. Accounts created via Google / phone OTP / admin have no password until one is set through the forgot-password flow — for them this returns a generic 401.

**Body**
- `email` — required
- `password` — required

Returns `{ status: "authenticated", tokens, user }`.

Verify a Google ID token minted by the frontend.

**Returns one of:**
- `status: authenticated` + `tokens` + `user` (existing customer, or a legacy/admin row adopted by email)
- `status: registration_required` + `registrationToken` + `needs: ["phone"]` (new customer — call **Register → Complete** with just the phone)

> ⚠️ **OTP verification is paused** while MSG91 is unavailable. New Google signups skip the OTP step entirely: collect the phone and go straight to **Register → Complete** (no `/otp/send`, no `otp` field). The phone is stored unverified until OTP is restored.

response.name: 200 Registration Required

request.description:
Send a login/signup OTP via MSG91. Same endpoint for sign-in and signup, so it never reveals whether the number is registered.

- `phone` — required. Any of `9112233445`, `+91 91122 33445`, `09112233445` normalize to the same E.164.

Rate limited per phone number (5 / 15 min) on top of the per-IP auth limiter.
Resend the current OTP. `channel` is `text` (default) or `voice`.

Verify the OTP.

**Returns one of:**
- `status: authenticated` + `tokens` + `user` (number already belongs to an account)
- `status: registration_required` + `registrationToken` + `needs: ["name","email"]` (new number — call **Register → Complete** with name + email)

> Dev without MSG91 configured: the OTP is `123456` (also printed to the server console).

response.name: 200 Registration Required

request.description:
Exchange a `registrationToken` for a real account + tokens.

**Send the fields the token needs:**
- Google token (`needs: ["phone"]`) — send `phone`. ⚠️ **OTP verification is paused (MSG91 down), so no `otp` is required; the phone is stored unverified.**
- Phone token (`needs: ["name","email"]`) — send `name` + `email`

Extra fields are ignored, so this single request body covers both.

response.name: 409 Already Registered

request.description:
Start a password reset. Always returns the same message so it never reveals whether the email exists. If it does, a reset link (Resend) is emailed with a token valid for 1 hour.

> Dev without Resend configured: the reset link/token is logged to the server console.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:

**Body**

- `password` — required, min 8 characters

**Body fields**
- `refreshToken` — required, string

**Body fields**

Confirm the new phone number with its OTP. Fails 409 if another account already uses it.

item.name: Addresses
item.description:
Customer billing address book. The default address supplies the place of supply used when an invoice is issued.

**How the state drives tax.** `stateCode` is the GST state code and is the *only* input to the CGST+SGST vs IGST decision. It is never inferred from the PIN code or the GSTIN.

StartupKaro supplies from Mohali, **Punjab (03)**:
- `stateCode` = `03` → intra-state → **CGST 9% + SGST 9%**
- any other code → inter-state → **IGST 18%**

The customer pays the same 18% either way — only the split changes. Note **Chandigarh (04) is inter-state** despite being next door.

Use `GET /customer/addresses/states` to populate the state picker.

request.description:
Reference data for the state picker. 37 GST state codes.

Codes 25 (Daman & Diu) and 28 (undivided Andhra Pradesh) are intentionally absent — both were retired (25 merged into 26, 28 reassigned to 37).
Default address first, then newest.

request.description:
All fields optional, but at least one must be present.

**Moving an address to another state.** `stateCode` decides the tax split on future invoices. If the address holds a GSTIN, the state is re-checked against it — so a relocation must send `stateCode` **and** the new `gstin` together. Sending either alone is rejected with 422:

```
{ "stateCode": "03" }   // 422 — existing GSTIN is still 06-Haryana
```

The example body above relocates the Haryana address created by *Add Address* to Punjab, swapping both fields at once.

`isDefault: false` is rejected on the current default: promote another address instead, so the customer is never left without one.

item.name: Invoices
item.description:
Invoices are issued **automatically when an order moves to `completed`**. There is no invoice before fulfilment.

Numbering is a gapless per-financial-year series (`SK/26-27/0001`). Party details and line items are snapshotted at issue time, so later edits to an address or the service catalog never alter an already-issued invoice.

All money is in **paise** (2950000 = ₹29,500.00).

request.description:
Invoices belonging to the signed-in customer, newest first.

All money is in **paise** (2950000 = ₹29,500.00).

**Tax split.** Indian states do not have different GST *rates* — the rate is uniform. What differs is the split, decided by the buyer's `stateCode` against Punjab (03):
- Punjab → `intra_state` → `cgst` + `sgst` populated, `igst` = 0
- elsewhere → `inter_state` → `igst` populated, `cgst`/`sgst` = 0

`taxableValue + totalTax == total` always holds, enforced by a DB constraint.

All money is in **paise** (2950000 = ₹29,500.00).
